messages:
maya: Heads up — customer ACME (hosted) reporting ~20% 503s starting ~07:02 UTC. They see timeouts and some payloads failing with upstream 500/segfaults. Pls triage, tagging oncall.

devin: @oncall-ops I'm seeing alerts too — spike in pod restarts on infer-pool-3 around 07:01. CPU fine, GPU memory went from ~78% to full in <30s, then container OOM + segfault.

anya: Any recent rollouts or model changes?

maya: We pushed a config change to enable KV prefetching for xlat/quant models at 06:45 as a canary (10% traffic). Could be related.

samir: copying logs from one of the crashed pods:
```
[2026-03-15 07:01:02] ERROR infer_runner: worker crashed: Illegal instruction (core dumped)
[2026-03-15 07:01:02] INFO coredump: pid=2456 signal=SIGSEGV addr=0x7f8b8f2c0000
[2026-03-15 07:01:02] ERROR gpu: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (allocated 113GB attempted 6GB)
```

julian: That memory spike looks like prefetch grabbed too much KV cache for long-context models. Canary might have hit a heavier prompt.

oncall-ops: Confirmed. Reproduced locally by running same workload against canary model variant (quantized + kv-prefetch). Memory climbs until OOM.

devin: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Disable kv-prefetch env flag for canary variant, 2) Route canary traffic back to stable model, 3) Increase GPU instance pool temporarily. Which do we want?

maya: Do 1 + 2 now. Push rollback for canary. Also set routing rule to fallback to model-stable-small if any node health checks fail.

samir: On it — running patch now. kubectl patch deployment infer-canary -n hosted --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"false"}]'

opsbot: deployment/infer-canary patched (revision 42 -> 43).

devin: Routing change: updating traffic weight to 0% canary via control-plane API: `curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/v1/route-adjust -d '{"pool":"infer-canary","weight":0}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN"`

opsbot: control-plane: traffic update accepted. canary weight=0%

anya: While we rollback, we should gather a reproducible minimal prompt + model hash to send to eng-runtime and eng-ml. Any large prompts from ACME?

maya: ACME sent an example — a ~12k token product catalog ingestion prompt. They were using streaming chat completions with long prefixes.

julian: That explains it. Prefetching KV for 12k contexts on quantized variant can expand KV cache significantly. We underestimated worst-case length.

samir: I've grabbed gdb backtrace from the coredump and uploaded to /tmp/artifacts/2098765432/backtrace.txt (internal link). Key frame: `at kv_cache_expand+0x12f`

devin: Flagging eng-runtime and eng-ml for postmortem. @julian @samir can you add reproducer + perf profile to the ticket?

julian: Will do. Quick workaround suggestion for customer: route their heavy jobs to model-stable-8k (smaller context) or enable server-side truncation to 8k.

maya: Notified ACME support: we applied rollback + routing fallback, asked them to test.

ACME (via support): Thanks — errors dropped to near-zero after ~2m. We'll monitor and let you know if anything else pops up.

oncall-ops: Current cluster status: pod restarts have stopped for infer-canary group, host GPU utilization stable. Rolling compute pressure back down.

devin: Action items: 1) eng-runtime to fix kv prefetch growth on quantized models, add guard caps; 2) eng-ml to run model-level worst-case mem estimates for prefetch; 3) product to add canary traffic limits for long-context prompts; 4) ops to add an auto-fallback route when pod OOM rate > X in 1m.

maya: I'll open incident ticket and schedule a quick blameless review. We'll include customer timeline and logs.

samir: Temporary hotfix also applied: `REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH_LIMIT=0.6` enforced on pool level to avoid full expansion until eng fixes landed.

opsbot: hotfix applied to pool infer-pool-3.

anya: ETA on root-cause PR?

julian: I'll have a draft PR by EOD with safe caps and a mem-estimation function.

maya: Great. Marking this thread resolved for now — reopen if ACME reports issues. Postmortem will live in #postmortems once ready. :white_check_mark:

devin: +1 — thanks everyone.

oncall-ops: Incident cleared at 07:09 UTC.

maya: Closing notes: customer impact limited to a handful of accounts, active mitigation succeeded, follow-ups assigned.
